q: A sequence ω is Martin-Löf random if:
opts: It passes every computable statistical test (every effective null hypothesis)
It has maximal Kolmogorov complexity at every prefix
It is normal in every base
exp: Martin-Löf (1966) defined randomness via algorithmic tests: ω is random iff it is not in any effective null set (measure-zero set definable by a computable process). Equivalently (Levin–Schnorr): prefix complexity K(ω₁…ωₙ) ≥ n - O(1) for all n.
